text:
Jamie: quick thought — can we move from hard rejects to a spillover/degrade-first admission for saturated GPU pools in eu-west?
Maria: sounds promising, what do you mean by "degrade-first" exactly? :thinking:
Jamie: instead of rejecting when queue > N, we push requests to a soft-path that runs cheaper quantized models or serves cached prefixes, and only reject when both queue and soft-path are saturated
Devon: curious about cost tradeoffs — degraded outputs still consume tokens and GPU cycles, so could blow budget if not throttled
Ryan: +1 to accounting, also need to ensure tail-latency SLOs don't get wrecked by saturation cascades across regions
Jamie: agreed. proposed rules: small warm pool + soft-path fallback per tenant. config sketch:
```
admit_policy: 
  threshold_queue: 80%
  degrade_first: true
  soft_path: [quantized-v1, cached-prefix-v2]
  max_soft_rate_per_tenant: 5rps
  hard_reject_after: 30s_of_backpressure
```
Sophia: max_soft_rate_per_tenant feels important — prevents noisy neighbors. how do we measure success?
Maria: metrics: soft_path_ratio, soft_to_hard_reject, p95_p99_latency, cost_per_token delta, customer_error_rate
Devon: also track quality regressions with a small eval set (sampled prompts per tenant) so we don't silently degrade correctness
Ryan: question on fairness: if soft-path uses lower-capacity models, do we prioritise premium tenants for fastpath? we should be explicit
Jamie: yes — priorities stay. soft-path is opt-in for premium tiers too (config per tenant). default: premium get longer queue budget and lower soft_rate cap
admit-bot: [automated] note: current eu-west GPU usage = 92%, queued = 4200, avg latency = 2.4s, warm_pool_fill = 60%
Maria: that's why we need this now. can we run a canary in a small AZ for 48h? monitor cost + p99 and also run a traffic replay to see quality delta
Devon: I'll wire a replay job against dev cluster and attach the eval harness. timeline: replay + small canary next Tue -> 48h -> review
Ryan: for rollout, suggest staged flags: 
  - feature flag to enable soft-path routing
  - telemetry flag to emit soft_path_reason on traces
  - kill switch to revert to hard-reject
Sophia: any network impacts? spillover might concentrate load on regional caches and KV stores — ensure we have WCU headroom
Jamie: good catch. add KV metrics to the dashboard and prewarm caches before flip
Maria: doc ask: can someone write a short runbook for ops — expected alerts, mitigation, how to revert? I can draft but need tech details from Devon
Devon: will add the replay results + config diffs to a PR. also pushing a stress test to simulate simultaneous 20% traffic spikes
Jamie: ok let's own tasks: Devon = replay + stress tests, Maria = ops runbook + dashboards, Ryan = rollout flags and canary plan, Sophia = capacity checks for caches, I'll coordinate PR and review
Maria: :thumbsup:
Sophia: :rocket:
Jamie: will post follow-up thread with canary start time once replay looks sane
admit-bot: [automated] created ticket INF-7423 for canary and replay artifacts
Ryan: thanks — leaning toward degrade-first if metrics look good and we keep hard-reject as final backstop
Maria: agree — lowers customer-visible failures while we get more capacity on deck
Devon: noted. will aim to have initial numbers by EOD Monday.
